chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Dharīḥ, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: Indeed, some people among the companions of Abī al-Khaṭṭāb delay the Maghrib until the stars become intermingled. He said: I dissociate myself before Allah from whoever does that deliberately.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being addressed in the report
key_terms.أَصْحَابِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ: followers of Abī al-Khaṭṭāb mentioned as practicing this delay
key_terms.بِالْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer, whose time is under discussion
key_terms.تَشْتَبِكَ النُّجُومُ: when the stars become densely visible or intermingled in the sky

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay maghrib prayer until the stars appear densely in the sky?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns deliberately delaying the maghrib prayer until the stars have spread out in the sky. It indicates a clear legal and religious disavowal of this intentional practice, marking it as contrary to the proper time of prayer.
